The story is partly sad,  people, you meet are crazy, hopeless, weird but others are by your side and help you with your task to find out, what had happened here in this town.  

Good thrilling story with excellent art style and music.  

Highly recommended!

This game is basically a cyberpunk "Hotline Miami" meets "Sonic the Hedgehog" with a not-annoying story line. For me, that checks a lot of boxes! I loved this game and everything it had to offer. 

For some, it will be frustrating to play a game with such a good aesthetic that is this difficult. Sure, I felt it was really rewarding to overcome combat rooms and tricky platforming lines, but that's not how everyone wants to spend their time. 

So before you pick it up, know that it's a game designed for you to fail... a lot! Luckily, it has a very quick restart and generous checkpoints, so the punishment for failure is not bad. Overall, I found the punishment worth it, as successful combat makes you feel *really cool* and the games look is just so well done. Looking forward to the sequel!

Dishonored is one of the best single player games I ever played. It came very close to the original Deux Ex for me. There are so many ways to play this game - pure stealth, pure combat or a combination of both. The game manages to take player decisions into account and change things in subtle and interesting ways. The powers and skills acquired allow different ways to approach mission objectives.

UI is customizable, and the game works fine on ultra wide resolution (3440x1440). I never experienced any technical issues. It also has quick save, quick load, auto save and manual save. A true PC game.

I highly recommend it.

Wolfenstein II is packed full of great and memorable moments, not only in the story it tells but also the combat it presents. From walking the streets of Roswell, New Mexico and seeing KKK members walking together with Nazis to sneaking up on an unexpected soldier only to gruesomely amputate and decapitate them before they could recite their favourite verse from Mein Kampf. 

It’s provocative and intense in equal measure. 

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Resident Evil Village masterfully blended horror and action to present another enthralling narrative the series is known for. As a casual gamer, I greatly appreciated the intuitive interfaces and straightforward mechanics, and while I initially doubted the effectiveness of its first-person perspective, I found it genuinely amplified the terror!

As for Shadows of Rose, it introduced some fresh scares, with a very gripping hide-and-seek sequence alongside a brilliantly designed multi-step doll puzzle. However, despite the 16-year gap, Rose's story felt far too anchored to the main narrative, stemming from its attempt to build an emotional connection through an underdeveloped relationship, by leaning heavily on a predictable father-daughter cliché, naturally leaving me quite disappointed at the lack of originality. :/

Very repetitive gameplay because of the time-loop, which I'm sure is intentional, but could have been executed better. Certain times it allows you to skip dialogue, even if you haven't seen it yet, but other times there will be long cutscenes and waiting periods that you can't skip. There are so many options and yet so many will just end the same way. I feel there could have been so much more to this game.
